summary: This script runs a directory listing command and processes its output line by line, printing each line to the console while simultaneously writing it to a log file with a timestamp. It sets up safety flags at the start to catch errors early, defines a logging function, and uses a pipeline to feed the command output through a loop.

explanations.2: These flags make bash exit immediately if any command fails (-e), treat undefined variables as errors (-u), and stop if any command in a pipeline fails (-o pipefail) — this prevents silent failures.
explanations.4: The -r flag makes this variable read-only, so it can't be accidentally overwritten later in the script.
explanations.6: The -r flag makes this filename constant throughout the script so it can't be changed.
explanations.7: Creating an empty file at that path ensures the file exists before we try to append to it; without this, the first write might fail or behave unexpectedly.
explanations.10: The >> operator appends to the file instead of overwriting it; the date command generates a timestamp, and ${line} is the content passed to this function.
explanations.14: The pipe (|) takes the output of the eval command and feeds it as input to the while loop below, processing it one line at a time.
explanations.15: IFS= means don't split on whitespace; read -r takes one line from the piped input without interpreting backslashes as escape characters.
